content.text:
- Retention windows: backups become eligible for review once they reach 90 days old (a more conservative window is 120 days) — age alone does not authorize deletion[^demo-backup-retention].  
- Safeguard — retention holds: any backup row marked retain: true must never be deleted and must be excluded from cleanup operations[^demo-backup-holds].

messages.content:
- Data availability: 120-day keeps ~33% more recovery points than 90-day (useful for uncovering late-discovered data issues or longer investigations); 90-day still covers most short-to-medium rollback needs for a demo environment.  
- Cost & operations: 120-day roughly increases storage/catalog and retention costs by ~33% (proportional to window) and slightly raises catalog/maintenance overhead; 90-day is materially cheaper and simpler to manage.  
- Risk/compliance & recommendation: unless the demo must meet regulatory/investigative requirements that demand 120 days, choose 90-day — it balances sufficient restore history with lower cost and operational overhead.

Research summary (comparing 90 vs 120 days, per the demo policy)
- Coverage: 120 days preserves about 33% more recovery points than 90 days, helping with late-discovered issues or longer investigations; 90 days still covers most short-to-medium demo rollback needs.  
- Cost & operations: 120 days increases storage and maintenance proportional to the longer window (roughly +33%); 90 days reduces storage and simplifies operations.  
- Risk & compliance: unless regulatory or investigative needs require 120 days, 90 days balances restore capability against cost and operational overhead.

Recommendation: pick 90 days for the demo unless you need the extra recovery coverage for compliance or forensic reasons.
